stories.headline: Fantasy baseball news and notes: Jac back for Royals, Twins promote top prospect
stories.summary: All of the important fantasy spin and actionable takeaways resulting from the latest baseball news.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Sept. 13: Sunday's news to know
By Todd Zola

It's another early Sunday start with the Detroit Tigers entertaining the Colorado Rockies at 12:10 p.m. ET. The usual 13 matinees follow, with the San Francisco Giants hosting the San Diego Padres in the evening affair.

The rubber game between the Boston Red Sox and Kansas City Royals at Fenway Park has been moved from 1:35 p.m. ET to 3:05 p.m. ET to avoid early afternoon storms in the area. The Royals could have Jac Caglianone returning to the starting lineup after he was able to pinch-hit in yesterday's contest. The slugger had missed the previous five games due to a left flexor strain.
The Minnesota Twins promoted top prospect Emmanuel Rodriguez in advance of yesterday's home date with the Cleveland Guardians. He responded by delivering a homer in his first career plate appearance. The 23-year-old outfielder generated a .262/.414/.500 line in his 49 games with Triple-A St. Paul. Rodriguez will likely play regularly down the stretch, but will also maintain 2027 rookie status.
The Texas Rangers lineup received a boost after the team activated Josh Jung from the IL. He's been out since just after the All-Star break thanks to a strained calf. Jung's return is timely as the Rangers sit just two games behind the Houston Astros for the AL West lead. They're also in play for the third AL wild card. Jung is batting .295/.362/.440, albeit in just 93 games.
The Athletics are playing out the string, but they'll be doing it with catcher Shea Langeliers serving as the team's DH. He underwent meniscus surgery in July, but the recovery went well. Even so, Langeliers isn't expected to play behind the plate again this season.
The Pittsburgh Pirates will be without Esmerlyn Valdez for at least 10 days and possibly the rest of the season, after placing him on the IL due to a left hamstring strain. The outfielder has emerged as one of the club's top run producers over the second half, though he'd been struggling lately. Even so, Valdez clubbed three homers and a double over his last 11 games, helping soften a 39% strikeout rate and a .154 average over that span.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Sunday.

Sept. 12: Saturday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's 15-game slate gets underway at 1:10 p.m. ET with the Detroit Tigers hosting the Colorado Rockies. Eight more matinees are staggered throughout the afternoon, with six evening games closing out the docket.

Jesus Luzardo has been scratched from today's start with a stiff shoulder. The Philadelphia Phillies are hopeful that he'll be able to make his next start. They plan on using a bullpen game today when they face the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park.
The San Diego Padres placed Ty France on the paternity list prior to last night's road game with the San Francisco Giants. He's eligible to be absent for up to three games. Mason McCoy was called up from Triple-A El Paso. Xander Bogaerts does not exhibit significant platoon splits, but it's still advantageous the first time facing a pitcher.
The Minnesota Twins announced that Byron Buxton is set for season-ending surgery on his right hip. He's been on the 10-day IL since late August, with top prospect Walker Jenkins taking over in center field.
Jac Caglianone was out of the Kansas City Royals lineup for the fifth consecutive game last night as he continues to nurse a left flexor strain. He's listed as day-to-day in advance of today's road tilt with the Boston Red Sox.
Yordan Alvarez missed last night's game between the Houston Astros and Tampa Bay Rays. Astros manager Joe Espada indicated that Alvarez is dealing with a right ankle injury, but they don't consider it serious, with a chance he returns for today's evening game with the Rays.

Sept. 11: Friday's Forecaster findings
By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Over the next 10 days of play, we're almost certain to see our first significant postseason berths clinched. The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers are virtual locks to assure themselves playoff berths (as a starting point) during the Sept. 11-13 weekend and several teams are within reach of celebrating during the upcoming week.

The Brewers (magic number of 5) and Los Angeles Dodgers (6) can clinch their respective divisions, and the New York Yankees (4), Dodgers (5), Atlanta Braves (8) and Boston Red Sox (9) can clinch wild-card spots, all of which seem likely to occur during fantasy's Week 24. From a player motivation standpoint, fantasy managers should prefer players from games with something on the line, and it's not uncommon for a team clinching some type of postseason berth or seeding to rest veteran players afterward, often in the game immediately following that happening.
The AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox visit the Cleveland Guardians, 1.5 games back in the division, for three games at Progressive Field from Monday through Wednesday.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Texas Rangers -- 1 and 2 games back in the AL wild-card race, respectively -- play three games at Globe Life Field from Friday through Sunday.
The Arizona Diamondbacks, 0.5 games back in the NL wild-card race, visit the Yankees, 3 games back in the AL East, from Friday through Sunday.
Fantasy managers could get boosts with the prospective returns of two injured hitters: Willson Contreras (hamstring) is on a minor league rehab stint and seems likely to be activated either at the start of or in advance of Boston's Week 24 road trip to Texas and Tampa Bay. Shea Langeliers (knee), once believed to be done for the season, is instead now on a minor league rehab stint and might begin to see some work as DH for the Athletics at some point during Week 24.
The Colorado Rockies play the entire week at Coors Field in one of only two weeks all season where they're scheduled for seven games there, and one of just four weeks played entirely at Coors. The Rockies do face a pair of talented pitching staffs in the San Diego Padres (4 games, Monday through Thursday) and Seattle Mariners (3, Friday through Sunday), but Coors' hitter-friendly confines nevertheless tilt things in favor of Rockies hitters in those matchups. Additionally, visiting Padres and Mariners hitters get to capitalize against Rockies pitching, which has baseball's worst ERA (5.50).

stories.headline: Why Baker Mayfield's contract means the QB market could burst
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield just got $55 million per year in new money -- which is telling about where the QB market is headed. That's great news for 11 other passers ready for big deals.
stories.body:
Fifty-five million dollars per year for Baker Mayfield? Seriously?!

Well, yes and no. Mayfield got his new deal from the Buccaneers on Tuesday, and it was a doozy. But it was also one of those win-win NFL contract outcomes where the player and agent get to brag about one number while the team gets to say, "Yeah, but ..."

Mayfield was already making $27 million in 2026. He now makes $37 million in 2026, $50 million in 2027, $50 million in 2028 and $55 million in 2029. That's four years and $192 million, which works out to $48 million per year over four years. But the "new money" in the deal -- money he didn't already have coming to him -- totals $165 million, and the Bucs added three years to his existing deal. Over three years, the average of $165 million is $55 million per year.

That's why both sides can claim victory and call it a win-win.

But you know who else comes out of this looking like winners? Every other quarterback who is or could be coming up for a contract extension within the next year.

Mayfield is a really good player. His career looked destined for an early end just a few years after he was the No. 1 pick in the 2018 draft, but he has found a home in Tampa, and it agrees with him. He has averaged 32 touchdown passes and 4,079 yards per season, and he won two NFC South division titles in three years with the Bucs. He has been good for them -- and they've been good for him.

But $55 million per year puts him in a tie with five other guys for third-highest average salary in the league. Dak Prescott makes $60 million per year. Patrick Mahomes' new-money average in his most recent deal was $64 million. Mahomes is the only quarterback who has even threatened -- let alone passed -- Prescott's salary in the two years since his deal was completed. Mahomes is also the only one with two MVP trophies, three Super Bowl titles and a 17-4 career playoff record. Mahomes is his own category.

The five who are tied with Mayfield at $55 million? Matthew Stafford (has won a Super Bowl and an MVP award), Joe Burrow (has been to a Super Bowl), Josh Allen (has won MVP), Jordan Love and Trevor Lawrence (uhh ... have excellent timing).

In eight NFL seasons, Mayfield has made two Pro Bowls, and his highest finish in MVP voting is 11th. His place is among the last two names in that previous paragraph, not the first three. But his presence there is what should finally make it a crossable threshold for the next group. Unlike Love and Lawrence, Mayfield wasn't benefiting from a red-hot extension market at the time he signed. This was a quiet year for top-of-the-market quarterback deals.

Mayfield had some leverage -- his contract was set to void three days after the Super Bowl and trigger an immovable $30 million dead-money cap charge for 2027 -- but the Bucs could have let him walk and trusted in their ability to find a good, affordable solution. You know, the way they did when Tom Brady retired and they signed Mayfield in the first place. The Buccaneers appear to have done this deal because Mayfield has been a really good quarterback for them, and this is what really good quarterbacks' contracts cost now.

This is fantastic news for anyone who considers himself a really good NFL quarterback and is (or will be) looking for a contract extension between now and next summer. And there are a lot of people in this category. The 2027 quarterback extension market could be the busiest we've seen in a while. And that is why 2027 should be the year when one or (likely) more quarterbacks try to join Prescott and Mahomes in the $60 million club. Many of them should, at least, get past the $55 million that we will now, for the purpose of this exercise, call the "Baker Line."

Here's a look at the quarterbacks in those conversations.

Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens
Jackson enters this season with two years left on his contract. He is making $52 million this year and is scheduled to make $52 million next year. The team approached him about an extension this past offseason, but nothing got done.

Jackson has tremendous leverage because his deal includes a clause that prohibits the Ravens from using the franchise or transition tags on him when he (hypothetically) becomes a free agent in 2028; it also has a no-trade clause. So, even if the Ravens couldn't get an extension done by next offseason and decided to trade Jackson rather than let him play out his contract year, he could pick his destination and veto any trade he didn't like.

Is he over the Baker Line? He is, by two MVP awards if nothing else. Jackson is the one guy in this group who already has a strong case to surpass Prescott's average annual salary of $60 million. It would be shocking and foolish at this point for him to agree to anything less. Imagine if Jackson were to stay healthy for two more years, play lights-out in both of them and become an unrestricted free agent in spring 2028 with no franchise tag to limit his earnings potential? What would he get ... $70 million per year? $80 million?

Drake Maye, New England Patriots
Entering his third year in the NFL, Maye will be eligible for a contract extension whenever the Patriots' season ends. Having finished second in MVP voting and led the team to the Super Bowl in his second season, Maye would have had a case to be over the Baker Line if he had been allowed to negotiate an extension this offseason. (CBA rules say you have to wait until after the player's third year.) The Patriots have a fifth-year option for 2028, which would buy them time next spring to work on this.

Is he over the Baker Line? Right now, probably. Mayfield has never been to the Super Bowl or placed second in MVP voting. If Maye were to suffer a significant injury or experience dramatic regression from his 2025 performance, he might be in a situation similar to the one C.J. Stroud is in right now, with the team picking up the option and waiting to see more before committing. But (Wednesday night's fourth-quarter meltdown aside) that feels unlikely.

Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears

Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders

Bo Nix, Denver Broncos
I'm grouping these three together because they're in very similar situations. Maye's 2024 first-round classmates have yet to reach the Super Bowl (which is why he got his own entry here), but each has shown plenty of the promise that led their teams to draft them where they did.

Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year and took the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game in his rookie season, then injuries derailed his second year. Nix helped the Broncos reach the AFC Championship Game last season, though he couldn't play in it because he broke his ankle during one of the final plays of Denver's overtime playoff victory over the Bills the week before. Williams struggled in his first year but really took off last season once the Bears hired Ben Johnson as their head coach. Williams didn't get to the NFC Championship Game, but the Bears took the Rams to overtime the week before in the divisional round.

All three of these guys can likely count on their teams picking up their fifth-year options next spring for 2028 if they can't get deals done before then. The other 2024 first-rounders were Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. and Minnesota's J.J. McCarthy, who don't yet merit much mention in a conversation like this.

Are they over the Baker Line? It depends. But given their credentials and accomplishments so far, each should get there as long as they show improvement rather than regression in Year 3.

C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans
The second pick in the 2023 draft had his fifth-year option for 2027 picked up in May, but he still hasn't secured an extension from the Texans, a team that is as proactive and generous as any in the league when it comes to veteran contract extensions. He was Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023 and has reached the second round of the playoffs every season he has been in the league. But his performance in last season's playoffs cost Houston a chance at the Super Bowl, and Stroud wisely appears to have decided he'd be better off negotiating next spring after a strong 2026 than doing it now.

Is he over the Baker Line? No, but he's betting on his own ability to get there. The Texans have Super Bowl hopes, with a championship-caliber defense that needs Stroud to play the way he did as a rookie. If he does -- and especially if they make a deep playoff run -- he'll be able to top not only Mayfield but also Prescott.

Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers
Young was picked one spot ahead of Stroud at the top of the 2024 draft, but he has not enjoyed the same level of success. He had a rough rookie season, then got benched for Andy Dalton early in his second season. Young recovered from that benching to finish 2024 strong, and he showed continued development in 2025, leading the Panthers to an NFC South title (albeit with an 8-9 record) and a playoff appearance in which Carolina gave the favored Rams a tough time before bowing out.

Similar to Stroud, Young was eligible for an extension this offseason but didn't get one. The Panthers clearly want to see more before committing long term.

Is he over the Baker Line? No, and this season would have to go incredibly well for both Young and the Panthers to get him there. Carolina picked up his fifth-year option for 2027, so there's no rush on this situation, which feels as though it could still go several ways.

Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia Eagles
Hurts signed his extension the same year Jackson signed his (2023). Hurts had just been to the Super Bowl and lost to the Chiefs. Two years later, he became a Super Bowl MVP and champion. Hurts has three years left on his contract, including 2026, at $51.5 million per year. This year's money is all guaranteed, as is $22 million of next year's salary.

The Eagles are coming off a disappointing season, especially offensively, and an offseason that saw them totally revamp their offense and trade away top wide receiver A.J. Brown. All eyes in Philadelphia are on whether Hurts can master new coordinator Sean Mannion's system and thrive in it.

Is he over the Baker Line? For sure. Hurts has been to two Super Bowls and won one. He has a 3.67 touchdown-to-interception ratio in his 10 career playoff games, of which he has won six. You can point out all of the flaws you want, but there's just no way an organization has the level of success the Eagles have had the past five years if the quarterback isn't good.

If Hurts were in a renegotiation now and demanded to make more than Mayfield, it would be hard to tell him he's wrong. But this exercise assumes he'll be in a renegotiation next spring, and there's no way to know how that will go until we know how this season goes. If Hurts flourishes in the new offense and the Eagles win a ton of games, he's likely to be in line for something in the $60-plus million range. If he flops and they miss the playoffs, it's not out of the question to think the Eagles would look to make a change. (Remember how Hurts got the job in the first place, so soon after they had extended Carson Wentz.)

If it's something in the middle -- offense starts slow, picks it up late and shows promise, etc. -- then Hurts and the Eagles probably figure out some kind of Band-Aid solution that puts off the big decision until after 2027. Fair or not, it feels as if there's a lot of pressure on Hurts this season to show once again that he belongs at the top of this market.

Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks
Darnold signed a three-year, $100.5 million contract with the Seahawks as a free agent in spring 2025. He had just helped lead the Vikings to a 14-3 record and a playoff appearance in 2024. And in his first year in Seattle, the Seahawks went 14-3 and won the Super Bowl.

No extension was offered to Darnold, who had already earned another $4 million in incentives last season based on performance and team success. He has $27.5 million in guaranteed money this year, and he's scheduled to earn another $35.5 million in 2027. The 2027 money is not guaranteed, though $10 million of it will become guaranteed if he's still on the Seahawks' roster March 15.

Is he over the Baker Line? Yeah, at this point, if you were his agent, you'd have to say he is, right? He has a 3-1 playoff record and a Super Bowl title. Mayfield is 2-3 in playoff games and has never advanced past the second round. You might think Mayfield is better, but these guys tend to get paid on what they've accomplished. And Darnold can make the case that he has accomplished more than Mayfield.

If the Seahawks have another good season, Darnold -- who left the season opener because of a hip injury, though it doesn't sound as though he'll miss too much time -- would be in line for an extension. He'd be quite the test case. The Seahawks have been pretty adamant about not overpaying quarterbacks, and their lack of action on a potential Darnold extension this offseason tells us they believe he's appropriately compensated.

But Darnold's deal with Seattle came one year after Mayfield's first extension with the Bucs, and the deals were almost identical. This time, Darnold and his agent should be able to point to Mayfield's contract again and say Darnold deserves at least as much. If that's the case, would the Seahawks do it? Or would they do what they did with Russell Wilson and Geno Smith when those guys asked for more than the team thought they were worth -- trade him?

Jared Goff, Detroit Lions
Goff got his extension in the offseason of 2024, when quarterbacks such as Lawrence and Tua Tagovailoa were getting contracts. Goff's came in at $53 million per year in new money -- just under what is now the Baker line. Goff has been to the Super Bowl with the Rams and got close with the Lions, who have a record of 50-35-1 in games he has started for them. Signed through 2028, he's set to earn $55 million this year, $40 million next year and $47 million in 2028. At this time, $18 million of his 2027 compensation is guaranteed.

Is he over the Baker line? Probably right on it, if not a little bit over. But this is another situation that likely depends on what happens this season. How the Lions feel about Goff and the state of their championship window in general next February will go a long way in determining how motivated they are to extend his contract, which has two years left, no matter how he plays at age 32.

Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings
Talk about a make-or-break year. Murray was owed about $37 million guaranteed from the Cardinals for this season. They released him, and that allowed the Vikings to sign him for a veteran-minimum $1.3 million and leave the Cardinals to pay the remaining $35.7 million. The Vikings have named Murray their starter ahead of 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy. Murray's contract includes a clause that prohibits them from using the franchise or transition tags on him next spring. So, if he has a huge year, they have no way of keeping him off the unfettered free agent market.

Is he over the Baker Line? No way, but that no-franchise clause is a whopper in terms of leverage. If Murray plays great and hits free agency next year at 29 years old, he'll sail past Mayfield -- and Prescott.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Chelsea to return for Roma star Koné
stories.summary: Chelsea are ready to reignite their interest in AS Roma midfielder Manu Koné. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
AS Roma midfielder Manu Koné is on the radar of Chelsea, while Bayern Munich are ready to pounce to sign Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz if there is a chance to do so. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are ready to reignite their interest in AS Roma midfielder Manu Koné when the transfer window reopens in January, as per Tuttomercato. However, the Blues may face competition from Liverpool this time around, who are keen on bolstering their midfield options. Koné was reported to be the subject of a €60 million offer from Chelsea at the end of August, which was swiftly rejected. The France international, who starred for his nation at this summer's World Cup, is under contract at Roma until June 2029.

- Bayern Munich are ready to pounce to sign Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz if there is a chance, says TEAMtalk. Wirtz, 23, moved to Anfield from Bayer Leverkusen for an initial €100 million in summer 2025 but has managed just five goals and three assists from 33 Premier League appearances so far. Bayern were interested in signing him last year and that hasn't changed now. Liverpool aren't looking to move on the Germany international right now, but that could change in the summer if his form doesn't improve.

- Barcelona were only willing to let left back Alejandro Balde leave permanently in the summer for €40 million, says Fabrizio Romano. Manchester United were one of the clubs who explored the possibility of signing the Spain international on loan, but Barcelona did not receive an offer. The 22-year-old is considered one of the top young defenders in Europe, but opted to compete for his place under Hansi Flick rather than push for a move.

- Liverpool have identified several midfield targets ahead of the January transfer window, with Monaco's Lamine Camara among their options, according to TEAMtalk. The Reds are also monitoring Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton and Inter Milan's Aleksandar Stanković (as was reported yesterday) as they look to add depth in central positions. Monaco are seemingly prepared to let Camara leave the club in January for €60 million, with the Senegal international keen on a move to the Premier League after his proposed €55 million switch to Chelsea collapsed.

- Roma are set to launch a bid to sign Real Madrid forward Endrick, Tuttomercato has revealed. Head coach Gian Piero Gasperini is a big fan of the Brazil international, 20, who enjoyed a successful loan spell at Lyon last term. But it remains to be seen whether Los Blancos will sanction Endrick's exit in January, however.

- Former Manchester United and Crystal Palace winger Wilfried Zaha has been offered to Málaga, with the Spanish club currently weighing up the proposal, Mundo Deportivo reports. The 33-year-old is without a club after leaving Galatasaray, having spent the previous two seasons with Charlotte FC in MLS. Málaga are exploring whether to replicate Deportivo La Coruña's successful swoop for Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, with former Manchester United forward Anthony Martial another free agent of interest.

Other rumors
- Arsenal are preparing to step up their interest in Como midfielder Nico Paz and could make a move in January. However, any deal will be complicated by Real Madrid, who retain an €80 million option to re-sign him in the summer of 2027. (El Desmarque)

- Barcelona are targeting Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck as they look to strengthen their defense. Hansi Flick has urged the club to move quickly for the Germany international, whom he handed his senior international debut to. (El Nacional)

- Dortmund wonderkid Samuele Inácio is on the radar of Juventus. The Serie A giants have already begun their pursuit of Inácio, who is under contract at BVB until 2029. (Tuttomercato)

- Sunderland are refusing to give up on Sporting CP winger Geny Catamo and could renew their pursuit in January. Sporting reportedly demanded an initial fee of €40 million, while Sunderland were prepared to offer €35m plus €5m in bonuses. (Record)

- German forward Lukas Nmecha is willing to leave Leeds United at the end of the season if he doesn't get more playing time. (Football Insider)

- Celtic are monitoring Liverpool left back Luke Chambers, who could become an option for the Scottish club in January. (Football Insider)

- Barcelona are preparing to offer forward Raphinha a contract extension that would keep him at the club until 2030. (AS)

- Panathinaikos have reached a verbal agreement with Roma over the signing of attacker Anass Salah-Eddine. (Footmercato)

- An unnamed UAE club have requested information on Juventus forward Arkadiusz Milik, who is out of favour in Turin. (Nicolo Schira)

- Despite reports to the contrary, Everton are not in talks to sign former Internazionale forward Mauro Icardi. (Nicolo Schira)

- Viking defender Jesper Daland is on the radar of several Bundesliga clubs, including Schalke and Eintracht Frankfurt. (Ekrem Konur)

- Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United are monitoring Internazionale youngster Aleksandar Stanković. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: Messi scores, but Nashville strikes late to deny Miami win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored a second-half goal, but Nashville SC struck back in stoppage time to earn a 2-2 draw at Inter Miami and maintain its nine-point lead at the top of the Eastern Conference.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi scored a second-half goal, but Nashville SC struck back in stoppage time to earn a 2-2 draw at Inter Miami and maintain its nine-point lead at the top of the Eastern Conference.

Messi looked to have given Miami the win when he exchanged passes with longtime Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul before picking out the side of the net with a precise left-footed finish from 20 yards out in the 62nd minute.

Twice Messi came close to extending Miami's lead and scoring what would have been his 100th for the MLS club in all competitions. But he was denied first by a Brian Schwake save onto the post and then by a last-ditch headed clearance by Nashville defender Jeisson Palacios.

Miami was then hit by a sucker punch in the first minute of added time when Sam Surridge fired Nashville level. Surridge had earlier put Nashville in front after just four minutes in South Florida.

Miami has now dropped 11 points from winning positions at home in MLS this season, second behind New York City FC and CF Montréal.

"Obviously, there's frustration -- feeling like we were the better side only to have the three points snatched away in the final moments," Miami defender Facundo Mura said. "But there's also the feeling that the team did manage to keep possession and create scoring chances.

"We need to improve so that we don't always have to score so many goals just to get the win; we need to feel a bit more secure at the back and stop conceding, so that the goals we do score are enough."

Saturday's dropped points could prove particularly costly, leaving Miami trailing Nashville by nine points in the battle for both the Eastern Conference's No. 1 seed and the Supporters' Shield with nine games remaining.

Nashville, which joined MLS as an expansion team alongside Miami in 2020, is now in prime position to claim its first Supporters' Shield.

Miami, which is still waiting for Cristian "Kily" González to formally take over as coach, has won just once in its past nine games in all competitions.

The team, and Messi, had plenty of chances to add to that win total Saturday.

Messi had a big hand in bringing Miami level in the 19th minute, when his in-swinging corner forced an own goal after it deflected into the net off the head of Nashville defender Reed Baker-Whiting.

Messi then had a shot blocked from outside the box in the 27th minute and sent a free kick wide shortly afterward before breaking through in the second half with his MLS-leading 19th goal of the season.

But the 39-year-old couldn't add to that total as he hit the crossbar as well as the post in the second half. Even after Nashville leveled in added time, De Paul was inches away from giving Miami the win when his shot hit the outside of the post.

Nashville is now unbeaten in four matches against Miami this season. In addition to winning 4-1 in the teams' previous MLS meeting on Aug. 15, Nashville also eliminated Miami from the Concacaf Champions Cup earlier this season.

After having also been eliminated from the Leagues Cup this summer, Miami will attempt to win its first trophy of the season when it takes on Cruz Azul on Wednesday in a battle between the reigning champions of MLS and Liga MX for the Campeones Cup.

"We have great players, and we have to compete for every trophy we play for," Mura added. "Unfortunately, things haven't gone our way in the Concacaf Champions Cup or the Leagues Cup. We haven't gotten the results we wanted; we're well aware of that. But ultimately, we're here to keep working and keep growing.

"We're starting a new phase with a new coach, and we all know we need to give more to help the team improve and reach a higher level -- especially since we have a final coming up in just four days that we really want to win."

ESPN's Lizzy Becherano, ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Cris Cyborg is still going strong as a force in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: At age 41, PFL women's featherweight champion continues win streak to secure spot in ESPN P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Cris Cyborg is an MMA legend. Period. End of story.

Actually, the Cyborg story continues, even with her being 41 years old and having spent 21 years in the sport. A champion in an unprecedented five fight promotions, she has long been a fixture in the ESPN pound-for-pound women's rankings. And by posting her 30th career victory -- the most ever by a woman in MMA -- at PFL Tampa on Saturday to retain the women's featherweight championship, Cyborg solidified her hold on the No. 3 spot.

It wasn't easy, not like so many past Cyborg fights in which she aggressively bowled over opponents to score quick knockouts. Ketlen Vieira put up a fight, bloodying Cyborg's face and achieving controlling positions on the canvas several times. But Cyborg persevered, nearly doubling Vieira's strike output and earning a unanimous decision win. As a result, the ESPN voting panel kept her right where she was in the top three.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Aug. 26. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko has more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and now she's established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 4

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

9. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber a must-win, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

UFC welterweight champion

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Where does Aspinall go from here?

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: USA-France gold medal game preview
stories.summary: It's the World Cup finale fans wanted to see: Team USA and France will meet in a rematch of the Olympic gold medal game.
stories.body:
It's the matchup everyone has been waiting to see.

The U.S. women's basketball team's mastery of international play was tested two years ago in Paris, during a one-point win over France in the Olympic final. In Sunday's FIBA Women's World Cup gold medal match (2 p.m. ET), the French hope to get their revenge.

Team USA beat Spain 76-66 on Saturday after France defeated host Germany 86-64 in Berlin. That leaves the top two teams to meet in the final. Since 1996, the United States has won every Olympic and World Cup gold except one: in the 2006 World Cup, when the Americans lost to Russia in the semifinals and took bronze.

France has been building as a national power, with 13 French players in the WNBA this season, including the Golden State Valkyries' Gabby Williams, who has dual citizenship and is a crucial player for Team France. She had 22 points and five rebounds Saturday.

The U.S. women had a slow start Saturday and led 39-36 at halftime. The score was tied 58-58 after three quarters. But Team USA took control in the fourth quarter, outscoring Spain 18-8. New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart had 16 points to lead the Americans, who had a big edge at the free throw line, going 27-of-35 to Spain's 10-of-11.

Can Team USA finish the job for its fifth consecutive and 12th overall World Cup gold medal? Or will France win its first? Here's how they match up and how each could win.

How France advanced

Voepel: Williams led four French players who scored in double figures and was also a big part of the defensive effort that forced Germany into 25 turnovers while France committed just six.

Germany trailed 25-23 after the first quarter. But France built its lead to seven at halftime, and with so many turnovers, Germany couldn't build a sustained comeback in the second half.

Williams' Golden State teammate Janelle Salaun had 14 points and 11 rebounds. Liberty guard Marine Johannes had 13 points, and Phoenix Mercury forward Valeriane Ayayi had 10. The French were outrebounded 41-31, but their huge turnover advantage overrode that.

The French have won their five World Cup games by an average of 35.6 points, with Saturday's 22-point margin the closest.

Philippou: I can't overstate how good France has looked this tournament. Though their group was not particularly strong, in the knockout rounds, the French crushed China and mostly had their way against Germany. They've had the best offense in Berlin, scoring 96.2 points per game, shooting 51.6% from the field and converting 44.2% of their shots from the 3-point arc -- hence Stewart's postgame comment that France is "shooting the s--- out of the ball." Those are numbers we are used to seeing from Team USA! And, of course, France's defensive identity is its foundation. Williams has been exceptional this tournament and looks determined to will her team to a historic gold Sunday.

How the USA advanced

Voepel: As was the case in Team USA's 55-52 victory over Italy in group play, the veterans took over to close out the win over Spain. Along with Stewart, Mercury guard Kahleah Copper (13 points) and Las Vegas Aces guard Jackie Young (12) scored in double figures.

The U.S. reserves contributed, though, with how they helped the Americans catch up after Spain's hot start. Indiana Fever center Aliyah Boston and Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers led the bench with six points each.

But with tensions high and the score tied going into the fourth quarter, the Americans relied on their players who have the most international experience to stay calm and make key plays in crunch time. Team USA had 15 turnovers in the game, but only one in the final quarter.

The Americans shot 40% from the field (23 of 58) and just 17% (3 of 18) from behind the arc. But their advantage at the line and their ability to hold Spain to 38% from the field (25 of 66) were enough to pull out the victory.

Philippou: The U.S. women finally found a semblance of rhythm in the fourth quarter, and it isn't a coincidence that was when they played their best defense of the game, holding Spain to just eight points. The execution on that end seemed to carry over offensively.

U.S. coach Kara Lawson primarily leaned on her vets late, though she gave Caitlin Clark a good run in that frame, and Boston played all 10 minutes.

"We had certain things we wanted to attack, and I thought we got to those in the fourth to score," Lawson said. "I thought defensively, it was the best we had played, from guarding the ball to guarding the ball screen to boxing out and limiting to one shot. Just every phase of defense, we were precise, and we were locked in.

"And so when we get all that going together, then we feel like we can create some separation. But our execution late, our shotmaking late, our understanding of mismatches late was all at a high level."

How do France-USA match up? What can we take away from the Olympic meeting?

Voepel: The French have not had a close game in this World Cup, and the Americans have had two. Based on how each team's five games in Berlin have played out so far, France has looked better. A possible advantage for the U.S. women is that they've had to dig deep and execute in crucial moments during their wins over Italy and Spain. So, perhaps that will help in what's expected to be a close matchup with the French.

It has seemed as though Team USA's offense has been feast (94 points vs. China, 105 vs. Czechia and 108 vs. Hungary), famine (55 vs. Italy) or frustrating (76 points vs. Spain, with USA taking too many bad shots and missing too many good ones). But the U.S. women are still where they expected to be against the foe they expected to face. Which Team USA offense will show up Sunday?

Looking back at the 2024 gold medal game in Paris, Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson, who is dealing with a back issue and isn't playing in the World Cup, led the Americans with 21 points and 13 rebounds. Copper and Kelsey Plum (also out of this tournament because of a leg injury) had 12 points in that game.

Williams led France with 19 points, seven rebounds and three steals -- and almost sent the game to overtime. She made a shot at the buzzer, but her foot was touching the 3-point line. That was the difference between playing an extra period for gold in Paris and leaving with a silver. It kept alive the United States' streak of eight consecutive Olympic gold medals.

Philippou: Lawson has said the sign of a good team is one that can win even when it's not making the shots it normally does. Still, the U.S.'s offense, at best, hasn't been consistent this tournament, and it feels more than likely Sunday could be another tough day for the unit against Les Bleues' defensive pressure.

"[The French] have great depth, they have great athleticism, and they found their style," said Olaf Lange, German national team coach and current associate head coach for the Toronto Tempo. "They're pretty much trying to jump every team with their pressure. ... We know from the Paris Olympics that this is also not easy to handle for USA. They probably have the tools, but they have way less chemistry than most international or European nations."

What could be Sunday's X factor?

Philippou: I'm fascinated to see how the psychological element of a gold medal game plays out and to observe how pressure impacts both teams. Marine Johannes said that France feels as though it has nothing to lose, but I'm not sure I buy that. There's clearly a desire to avenge the Olympic loss, and even some pressure to finally get French basketball on top.

"All we care about is winning," Dom Malonga said after the quarterfinal. "The French national team has been known for years for like second place or semifinals, never all the way, even in EuroBasket, until now. I feel like we have to do it. We have to make it happen."

France also doesn't have as much experience in these moments as the United States. At the same time, the U.S. has six players who haven't played at the World Cup or Olympics. And yet, the pressure the players face is to avoid being the team that ends the Americans' run, while also, as Stewart noted, keeping emotions in check.

"[The pressure] is constant," Stewart told ESPN. "Team USA, we haven't lost a World Cup game since '06. The same with the Olympics, however many gold medals in a row. It's not bad pressure. It's just the standard of what we do here. But it's like, we have to know what we're protecting and know what we're chasing.

"You can't shy away from it. You just have to embrace it. Like, this is the standard. This is the standard that those before me put into place, and now, we make it the standard, and we just continue to keep it."

Voepel: The Americans could help themselves if they can hit more 3-pointers. They struggled there Saturday, and it impacted their offensive effectiveness. The United States made 12 3-pointers vs. China and Hungary, one vs. Italy, seven vs. Czechia and three against Spain.

By contrast, France has been much better from behind the arc, making at least 10 3-pointers in every game with a high of 22 (on 40 shots) in its 111-56 win over Nigeria on Monday. The Americans will need to slow down France from long range while also shooting better.

stories.headline: Fenerbahce coach returns to work after resignation confusion
stories.summary: Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.

Kartal had announced he was quitting his role following Thursday's draw against AS Roma in the Champions League but the club refused to accept his resignation.

Kartal, nevertheless, failed to attend training on Friday ahead of a Superlig game against Gaziantep FK.

However, Fenerbahce released a statement late Friday saying Kartal would resume his duties on Saturday for the Super Lig match against Gaziantep on Monday.

On Saturday, the club's official X account showed photos of him at work.

Kartal had resigned to the surprise of the club and its players in his news conference following the 1-1 draw with Roma to begin the Turkish club's Champions League season.

"First of all, I congratulate my players for carrying out the tasks I assigned for tonight's match to the letter. We played football worthy of the Champions League," the state-run Anadolu Agency quoted Kartal as saying on Thursday. "We could have won the match; we had clear chances. The match ended in a draw, and I am proud of my players."

Kartal continued: "Tonight, I am resigning from my position -- never to return. I extend my heartfelt thanks to my players."

In a separate news conference soon after, club chairman Aziz Yildirim said Fenerbahce fans had hurled a water bottle at Kartal, describing the incident as a reason for the coach's decision. Kartal was also upset by a series of social media posts, Yildirim said.

Yildirim insisted that Kartal's resignation was not accepted and that he would remain at the helm.

"You saw the state Ismail was in. Can a person endure that much distress?" Yildirim said. "They threw a water bottle at Ismail Kartal's head. We saw it. That is why he is upset."

"Ismail Kartal remains in his post," Yildirim added. "I said [to Kartal]: 'You will continue,' and that was that."

Despite reports in Turkey that Fenerbahce official Oguz Cetin later met with Kartal but failed to convince him to stay, Kartal is now set to take charge of the team's fixture against Gaziantep FK on Monday.

Fenerbahce is 11th in the 18-team league.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen says F1 should consult drivers on new circuits amid Spanish Grand Prix concerns
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has called on Formula 1 to consult drivers when designing new circuits amid concerns there will be no overtaking at Sunday's inaugural race at the all-new Madring.
stories.body:
MADRID -- Max Verstappen has called on Formula 1 to consult drivers when designing new circuits amid concerns there will be no overtaking at Sunday's inaugural race at the all-new Madring.

This year the Spanish Grand Prix has moved to Madrid on a new hybrid street circuit featuring 22 corners and multiple high-speed sections.

Verstappen qualified his Red Bull third on the grid -- behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris on pole position -- but doubts there will be any opportunities to move up the order after the start.

"It will be tough, I mean, let's say best case scenario and you're faster [than the car in front], you still can't pass," he said.

"There are no corners where you can pass, so you need to rely on people degging [suffering tyre degradation] very aggressively. So yeah, it's going to be tough.

"I mean, in the long runs it was very tough with a lot of deg for everyone, so that will be probably the key point tomorrow. But even with that, I need to still figure out a corner where you can pass."

Turn 5 has been highlighted as the best overtaking opportunity, but the curved braking zone on the approach to the slow-speed chicane means the lead driver can easily defend by positioning their car in the middle of the track.

What's more, Verstappen said the combination of braking and turning in an F1 car makes the challenge of overtaking even more difficult.

"The corners, like I said before, you can't overtake," he added. "So, in some places, the braking zones, they need to learn that it should never be that you have to steer and combine with the braking because it doesn't allow any kind of overtaking. So, for sure, in terms of track design, I think it can be better."

- McLaren's Lando Norris pips Kimi Antonelli to take thrilling pole for Spanish Grand Prix

- Will Madring live up to reputation as F1 car killer? 'The most risky circuit of the calendar'

- Carlos Sainz hit with three-place grid penalty for home Spanish Grand Prix

Verstappen questioned why F1 track designers do not consult current drivers on circuit designs, saying there are always ways to promote overtaking on a completely new layout.

"I think also input from drivers in the future on track design can also help a lot," the four-time champion said.

"I know they will always come back to you and say 'yeah, but the space [is not available].' Yes, but there's always a way to find an overtaking opportunity around a track.

"But, overall, the event itself is very cool. I mean, yes, they've done a great job. Also, how quickly they made the track available, the information that was shared for the simulator. So, in that sense, I think it was very good.

"But, in terms of if you want to have better racing, overtaking, I think there can be a few corners that can be changed."

Verstappen also said the circuit's signature corner -- the banked La Monumental -- had not lived up to expectations in qualifying due to the need to preserve battery energy for later in the lap.

The Red Bull driver has been one of the biggest critics of F1's new engine formula for 2026, which requires nearly 50% of peak power to be derived from the car's battery pack.

Verstappen said he had looked forward to the corner prior to arriving in Madrid, but was unable to take it flat out for fear of draining the battery.

"Well, I wanted to go flat, but then my battery died," he said. "I had to add a lift, to have better deployment [of energy further around the lap].

"So that's my La Monumental experience.

"Yeah, I mean, it's cool, the banking, but I think they should have done it the other way around, though -- initially more banking and then just flatten it out.

"But in an F1 car you have so much downforce. I think it's more challenging in the other categories [Formula 2 and Formula 3] because it didn't look so easy flat in other categories.

"For us, plus because our battery dies towards the end, so you already slow down a bit. But, I mean, I guess for the shots it looks great from the outside."

stories.headline: Golden Knights extend Mark Stone with 2-year, $18M deal
stories.summary: Golden Knights captain Mark Stone has signed a two-year contract extension with a $9 million annual value that goes through the 2028-29 season.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Golden Knights captain Mark Stone signed a two-year contract extension Saturday with a $9 million annual value that goes through the 2028-29 season.

He will make $9.5 million this season in the final year of his current deal.

Stone, 34, is coming off a season in which he totaled a career-high 73 points (28 goals, 45 assists) for a Golden Knights team that advanced to the Stanley Cup Final before losing to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games.

Known for boisterous goal celebrations, Stone is the emotional driver behind the Golden Knights, having played in 400 career games for the club. He also has produced, scoring 136 goals with 260 assists and a +112 rating.

Stone has 259 goals and 448 assists over a 15-year career, including more than six seasons with Ottawa before his trade to Vegas on Feb. 25, 2019.

Injuries have kept Stone from delivering even more, but he has played in at least 60 games each of the past two seasons. If Stone can stay healthy, especially going into the playoffs, the Golden Knights could make another deep postseason run with roster that includes Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner.

stories.headline: What we learned: Selfless Lions maul Crows to leave Hawks shaking in their boots
stories.summary: From 53-point losers to 53-point winners, nobody rebounds like Brisbane. The three-peat is firmly on track.
stories.body:
GABBA -- Brisbane thrashed Adelaide on Saturday evening to book a fifth consecutive AFL preliminary final berth and send a major warning to the league's remaining finalists that its three-peat is firmly on track.

The Lions rebounded in style from last week's humbling defeat in Sydney and will now face Hawthorn at the MCG for a place in yet another Grand Final.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

The Lions are just two wins away from a magical dynasty ... and who would bet against them?
No team knows how to shake off a difficult loss quite like Brisbane. The Lions couldn't have played worse if they tried in last week's 53-point qualifying final defeat to Sydney at the SCG. The Swans, fresh off one of the most difficult fortnights in club history, caught lightning in a bottle and had the reigning champs rattled in the opening minutes. All of Brisbane's prime movers were well below their best and at no stage did they look like working their way into the contest. But that was last week.

Seven days later the Lions side showed why they are the back-to-back reigning premiers, bouncing back in emphatic style to record a 53-point win of their own, a crushing defeat of Adelaide to once again book a place in the last four. Brisbane flew out the gate, enjoyed the first 10 inside 50s of the night and put five goals on the Crows in just seven minutes and 13 seconds. By quarter-time it was 42-15 -- the Lions' highest score in the first quarter of a final since 1999.

So many of Brisbane's stars bounced back from their poor outings the week before. Charlie Cameron was electric with five goals. Zac Bailey, fresh from an eight-year contract extension during the week, kicked three goals from his 23 disposals. Kai Lohmann and Cam Rayner provided headaches in the front half all night. Will Ashcroft returned to finals Will Ashcroft (more on him later).

The ability to immediately respond has been an enviable trait of Brisbane over the past 12 months. Last year, the Lions were also humbled in a road qualifying final. They then won their next three finals to lift the premiership cup. In fact, since 2022 this club is now 11-2 in win-or-go-home finals.

Even this year the Lions have been quick to make amends for their most inexplicable losses. A 44-point defeat to the Swans in Round 1 was followed by a 33-point win against the Saints. The 76-point loss to the Blues late in the season was followed by a 67-point crushing of the Hawks. Even the rough three-game stretch midyear that had the footy world questioning their hunger was followed by wins in 10 of their final 11 home-and-away games.

The Lions will now travel to the MCG to battle Hawthorn for a place in a fourth consecutive Grand Final. Just two wins separate this resilient club from a stunning three-peat, are you brave enough to tip against them?

Despite the reports and the blowout, Matthew Nicks should remain safe in his role
Adelaide's finals road came to an abrupt end on Saturday evening in Brisbane. It's a loss that will no doubt sting for some time, but there's certainly no shame in falling to the back-to-back reigning champs on their home deck, right?

The Lions were clearly the better side on the night but the difference really was the burst in the opening minutes and another similarly scary attacking onslaught midway through the second term.

Perhaps Adelaide threw its biggest punch last week against the Bulldogs after rumours began circulating that coach Matthew Nicks could be out of a job should his side fail to win the home elimination final. That seemed wildly unfair at the time and even more ridiculous now they've taken it up to Brisbane.

There should be absolutely zero pressure on Nicks. At the end of the day, a coach's job is to win games. Since the beginning of last year, Nicks has orchestrated 34 wins. Only Brisbane's Chris Fagan, Geelong's Chris Scott, and Fremantle's Justin Longmuir boast more in that time. The Crows have also only suffered two heavy defeats in that period (one of them was tonight). For reference, Brisbane's had seven. Anyone who has built that type of enviable record over a two-year period deserves, at the very least, the respect of not being made to feel as if they're on the coaching hotseat.

Why is there this unfair expectation that Nicks and the Crows should be achieving so much more than they are? Even the most one-eyed Adelaide supporter would concede this side's probably not a top three team on paper, so finishing the season in fifth or sixth place should hardly be considered a failed campaign. Until the Crows are heading backwards, Nicks should not have to worry about his job security.

Will Ashcroft really should have been an All-Australian over Murphy Reid
Two-time Norm Smith Medal winner Will Ashcroft etched the latest chapter into his remarkable finals legacy on Saturday evening, turning in a dominant display against the Crows to propel Brisbane into yet another preliminary final.

It continues a dominant season for the young Lion who is not only the bookmakers' favourite to be best on ground on Grand Final day for a third time in succession, but is widely tipped to finish in the top five of this year's Brownlow Medal count. And yet, amazingly, Ashcroft wasn't selected in last month's All-Australian team.

Second year Docker Murphy Reid was someone who did receive a blazer. So, let's compare the pair:

You be the judge of who deserved to be included in the prestigious team.

Both Reid and Ashcroft were unusually quiet in their side's qualifying final losses last week. Both lifted on semifinal weekend, but Ashcroft's 30 disposals, 13 score involvements, six clearances, seven inside 50s, seven marks, and almost 500 metres gained against the Crows were just about best on ground numbers. And while finals performances don't count towards the All-Australian team, Ashcroft's latest outing only highlights how much of a blunder it was not having him in the 2026 team.

stories.headline: 'God no': Penrith say Cleary should avoid ban after hit
stories.summary: A defiant Ivan Cleary insists his superstar son Nathan should not face a ban for dangerous contact, after the Penrith star went from villain to hero in the Panthers' 19-12 finals win over the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
A defiant Ivan Cleary insists his superstar son Nathan should not face a ban for dangerous contact, after the Penrith star went from villain to hero in the Panthers' 19-12 finals win over the Sydney Roosters.

In a cracking Sunday afternoon qualifying final, Cleary was sin-binned for collecting Hugo Savala's leg before breaking a 12-12 deadlock with a late field goal at CommBank Stadium.

Adding to the drama, the Penrith No.7 also injured his foot in the process of landing the dropkick, seeking the attention of trainers before opting out of taking the conversion attempt after Brian To'o's late try.

The result means the Roosters will host Cronulla in a do-or-die semi-final on Saturday night, while Penrith are one win away from their sixth grand final in seven years.

But all eyes will be on the NRL's charge sheet on Monday, with Cleary anxiously awaiting what sanction he will face for crashing into Savala's leg after the Roosters player kicked in the first half.

The Panthers star immediately gave a worried look, before referee Gerard Sutton told him his action had "force", was "very dangerous" and "carried a high risk of injury".

"He's just trying to make a play. He's probably thinking the right thing there," coach Ivan Cleary said.

"The angle was wrong and under the current rules it's probably the right call.

"The same thing happened to him down the other end under the posts early in the game, but anyway."

If Nathan Cleary was to receive a grade-two dangerous contact charge on Monday, the game's best player would be facing a ban from the preliminary final with an early plea.

Should he elect to challenge the charge, he would risk being rubbed out of the grand final if found guilty.

A grade-one charge would only attract a fine for Cleary, and prove a massive boost in Penrith's bid for a fifth premiership of their dynasty.

Asked if he felt the halfback deserved a ban over the contact, Ivan Cleary said: "God no. Of course not.

"He just got the wrong angle. It's one of those rules that has come in over the past couple of years and sometimes in the heat of the battle you forget.

"He's not injured. It's just a black-and-white thing they have brought in."

Manly's Josh Aloiai and South Sydney's Jacob Host were handed grade-two charges by the match review committee for collecting the outstretched legs of kickers in 2024.

But Melbourne's Harry Grant did manage to have a grade-one charge for contact on Dan Atkinson overturned that year.

The Roosters failed to make use of Cleary's sin binning. Savala missed the ensuing penalty goal and was denied a try for a double movement after the break.

That was one of the few chances during a scoreless opening 32 minutes of the second half, before Cleary stepped up as the game's ultimate ice man.

Sat in the attacking line after a searching Moses Leota run, Cleary was able to slot over the one-pointer with no pressure from Roosters defenders.

"I would have liked to have put more pressure on him," Roosters coach James Tedesco said.

"But it was just a quick play-the-ball and a quick ruck."

Daly Cherry-Evans attempted to reciprocate moments later, but sprayed a shot from 20 metres out to the right before To'o's sealer under the posts.

Cleary's boot also wreaked havoc early on Sunday, with the Roosters unable to handle three of his bombs and Liam Martin leaping to score off one of his shallow cross-field kicks.

Cleary also changed the point of attack and went back inside to Dylan Edwards for the Panthers' second try, with the fullback swerving his way over to make it 12-12 after 38 minutes.

Mark Nawaqanitawase's freakish ability had kept the Roosters in the match in the first half, with two key intercepts either side of a Robert Toia try.

The Roosters winger first helped deny a Penrith try when he reached out and held onto an Isaiah Papali'i ball in the third minute.

He then gave the Roosters a 12-6 lead when he stretched out to stop a Penrith break, juggled the ball three time as he fell, got up and ran 45 metres to score.
